title: Jurisdictional escalation scenarios and customer scriptbook
content:
Purpose and scope
This working doc collects a small set of realistic escalation scenarios involving jurisdictional or cross-border data requests, region-pin enforcement failures, and audit evidence demands. The goal is to provide concise operator decision points and customer-facing message templates (scripts) so support/SEs can move fast without over-committing.

Audience
- Tier 1/2 Support engineers, Solutions Engineers (SEs), Oncall Operators
- Regional ops leads and Eng SREs
- Legal & Compliance liaisons for partner escalation

High-level escalation matrix (one-line)
- L1 (Support): initial intake, triage, collect metadata, quick signals (<= 2 hours)
- L2 (Ops/SE): verify routing/pinning, reproduce failure, gather logs and evidence (<= 8 hours)
- L3 (Legal + Engineering lead): evaluate legal request validity, produce audit bundle, coordinate customer comms (<= 48 hours)

Scenario A — Subpoena or lawful request naming tenant data (no immediate outage)
Trigger: Customer or third-party legal notice referencing content from tenant X; customer requests evidence of data locality and retention.
Operator steps (L1 -> L3):
- L1: assign ticket, capture uploaded notice (redact PHI locally), ask customer for tenant id and time window, confirm contract pinning scope.
- L2: run routing query: region_assertion logs + last-processed-edge-zone for tenant id; pull region-pin config snapshot (pin record + model routing override list). Save request headers and request IDs.
- L2: snapshot KV / prefix-cache entries and storage SLA metadata for the requested timeframe. Create a chronological evidence list (what we can prove, what we cannot).
- L3: Legal review to confirm validity and prepare limited disclosure. Assemble audit bundle (signed manifest describing sources of truth, hashes of logs, chain of custody notes).
Customer script (initial response) — send within 24 hours:
Subject: Received notice — Redwood next steps to gather evidence
Body: Hi <customer_name>, we received your notice and are assembling the requested locality evidence for tenant <tenant_id>. Next steps: we will (1) pull routing logs and region-pin records for the timeframe you specified, (2) prepare a signed audit bundle for you and any designated legal recipients. Expected ETA: 48–72 hours. If you can provide the exact time window and any request IDs referenced in the notice it will speed things up.

Scenario B — Region-pin enforcement failure (requests routed out-of-region)
Trigger: Customer monitoring fires, or SLO telemetry shows requests serving from non-authoritative region for pinned tenant.
Operator steps:
- L1: open incident, tag affected tenant(s), collect example request IDs and request traces. Put temporary throttling or routing hold if repeated leakage confirmed.
- L2: run quick checks: config drift (pin config vs. service config), edge-zone mapping, last deploy touching routing policy. If easy rollback exists, execute controlled rollback to previous routing config and validate with synthetic test traffic.
- L2: if rollback not possible, enable temporary gated fallthrough to 'nearest pinned region' and record user-visible change. Capture telemetry: percent of traffic out-of-region, affected model types, time window.
- L3: notify Legal/Customer Success for customer-facing incident report and SLA implications.
Customer script (initial incident update):
Subject: Incident — temporary routing deviation for tenant <tenant_id>
Body: Hi <customer_name>, we detected a routing deviation impacting requests from your tenant. We have scoped the impact and are executing a mitigation (either config rollback or temporary fallback to the nearest pinned region). We will share a post-incident report within 72 hours including affected request IDs and remediation. Apologies — we recognize residency guarantees are critical and are prioritizing this.

Scenario C — Cross-border fallback required for emergency availability (legal/compliance-sensitive)
Trigger: catastrophic capacity loss in a pin region (zone down) requiring temporary failover to different geography to keep critical flows live. This is high-sensitivity — requires documented approvals.
Operator steps:
- L1: identify impacted customers and flag any with hard pin requirements (contract exceptions).
- L2: consult the emergency fallback policy — ensure approvals chain is satisfied (customer consent if contract requires, or legal-authorized emergency protocol). Capture the list of affected tenants and fallback destinations.
- L3: produce an emergency approval note: \"reason, risk, timeline, assets affected, rollback plan, data handling constraints.\" Store approval in case system. Proceed only after required sign-offs.
Customer script (pre- fallback outreach template — send before failover when possible):
Subject: Urgent — temporary regional fallback proposal for availability
Body: Hi <customer_name>, an outage in region <A> is impacting availability for tenants in that region. To avoid prolonged downtime we propose a temporary failover to region <B>. This will route requests through <B> for up to <X hours>. We will: (1) log all requests and provide an audit bundle after failover; (2) revert routing as soon as <A> is healthy; (3) honor any deletion/retention instructions that apply. Please reply with approval or questions; if we do not hear back within <Y hours> we will follow emergency protocol described in your contract.

Evidence collection checklist (common to all scenarios)
- ticket id and uploaded notices/attachments (PDFs)
- tenant id, org id, account owner contact
- exact time window (start/end timestamps)
- example request IDs + full request traces (headers, source IPs, region assertion tag)
- region-pin config snapshot + commit PR id (if applicable)
- routing rules, edge-zone map version, deploy id (git sha)
- storage / object metadata (s3 location, bucket region, object write timestamps)
- hashes of logs (sha256) and chain-of-custody note (who exported, when)
- signed audit manifest (pdf) and list of files included

Operator quick queries and saved searches (notes for L2)
- Find routing traces by tenant: query logs for tenant_id=%s and filter delta from pinned_region.
- Check pin config: /api/internal/pinning/v1/tenants/%s/snapshot (record output file id).
- Edge-zone map: edge_map_version from config service and compare to runtime agent.
- Telemetry: percent_out_of_region_by_hour(tenant=%s) and tokenized_request_samples(limit=50).
Note: keep queries idempotent and avoid exporting PII in broad queries. Use narrow windows.

Communications policies and tone guidance
- Maintain neutral, factual tone: acknowledge, state observable facts, next steps, ETA.
- Do not speculate about legal compliance outcomes. Deflect to Legal for requests to opine on validity.
- When in doubt, escalate to L3 early — do not promise audit artifacts until Legal signs off.

Sample email templates (short)
1) Acknowledgement (automated or manual):
Thanks — we received your request. We're triaging with engineering and legal. We'll follow up with an ETA within 24 hours and a point of contact.

2) Evidence delivery note (after Legal approves bundle):
Subject: Audit bundle for request <request_ref> — tenant <tenant_id>
Body: Hi <recipient>, attached is a signed audit bundle containing routing logs and pin config snapshots for the requested timeframe. The bundle includes a manifest that explains sources and limitations. If you need additional artifacts, please send a formal request and point of contact for validation.

Unresolved questions / decisions to make (ops backlog)
- Define exact retention policy for routing traces used in audits (current retention 90 days — should we extend to 180 for enterprise customers?).
- Agreement on signed audit manifest template (format and fields) — Legal to finalize.
- Automate export tooling so L2 can create tamper-evident bundles without manual steps.
- Clear per-customer contract flag: "emergency-fallback-consent" to avoid ambiguous approvals during incidents.

Playbook maintenance notes
- Owner: Aisha Patel (ops) + Priya Gupta (Legal).
- Review cadence: quarterly or after any major incident involving cross-border fallback.
- Place canonical documents and signed templates on Confluence and link to customer-facing runbooks for SEs.

Appendix — quick scripts for Slack/phone escalation
- Slack to Legal: @legal-urgent \"Need OOO sign-off for emergency regional failover for tenant <tenant_id>. Impact: <# tenants>, reason: <region outage>, timeline: propose <X hours>. PRD: <link>.\"
- Phone script for oncall lead (30s): \"Hi — we have a region <A> outage affecting a set of pinned tenants. Legal may need to approve temporary failover to <B>. Please standby for ticket <id> with evidence. Will follow up with approval call.\"

End notes
This is intentionally compact — primary intent is a living operator scriptbook that reduces decision latency. Please add real incident examples below as we go (redacted) so templates become richer and cover edge cases.
